dimensions.assessment: Affects State officers and employees administering covered benefit programs and individuals prosecuted for covered fraud offenses.
dimensions.evidence: To impose liability on State officers and employees who fail to prevent fraud, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Substantial and potentially life-changing penalties, including personal financial liability up to three times aggregate loss without immunity, and mandatory minimum prison sentences ranging from 1 year to life.
dimensions.evidence: not less than 1 year in prison, and not more than life.

dimensions.assessment: Civil damages recovered from State officers/employees and potential impact on state and federal correctional expenditures due to mandatory minimum sentences.
dimensions.evidence: damages in an amount not exceeding 3 times the amount of aggregate loss resulting from such violation.

dimensions.assessment: Amends Title 18 of the United States Code to add mandatory minimum sentencing tiers and establishes a new federal civil action against State personnel.
dimensions.evidence: Subchapter A of chapter 227 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 3559 the following

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory changes to criminal sentencing law and civil liability rules for state benefit administration.
dimensions.evidence: with respect to criminal conduct that occurred after the date of enactment of this section

missing_information: Expected number of prosecutions or civil actions brought under these provisions.
importance_detail.rationale: Imposes personal civil liability on State officers and employees who fail to prevent fraud in covered federal-state benefits programs, and establishes strict mandatory minimum federal prison sentences for certain fraud offenses.
